{{Quote|With the ''Executor'' under my command, ''I'' will be the ultimate power in the universe!|Kendal Ozzel, moments before his execution|<ref name="New Vehicles & Vessels">''[[The New Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]''</ref>}}
'''Kendal Ozzel''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] born into a wealthy [[Carida/Legends|Caridan]] [[Ozzel family/Legends|family]]. After studying at multiple [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core World]] military institutes, Ozzel graduated as a [[Captain of the Line/Legends|Captain of the Line]] but was relegated to teaching positions because his superiors had doubts about his ability to serve as an effective field [[Commander/Legends|commander]]. Nonetheless, at the advent of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], Ozzel was commissioned as a [[Captain/Legends|captain]] in the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] by [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] and went on to serve with the [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone]] forces in multiple engagements. He continued to serve under now-[[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] Palpatine when the Republic was [[Declaration of a New Order|reorganized]] into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the Confederacy was crushed.

Ozzel was eventually assigned as the captain of the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] [[Reprisal (Imperial II-class)|''Reprisal'']], but he longed for a promotion to [[Admiral/Legends|admiral]]. As commanding officer of the ''Reprisal'', he oversaw campaigns against the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] in the [[Shelsha sector/Legends|Shelsha sector]]; on one such mission, Captain Ozzel became involved in a plot to [[Death/Legends|kill]] [[Emperor's Hand/Legends|Emperor's Hand]] [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]] when he erroneously believed her arrival aboard the [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] was part of a high-level investigation into the desertion of a [[Hand of Judgment|group of stormtroopers]]. Jade became suspicious of the captain, finding him to be either disloyal or dim-witted, and recommended that the [[Supreme Commander (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Supreme Commander]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], keep an [[Eye/Legends|eye]] on him. [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Naval]] [[Imperial High Command/Legends|command]] ultimately agreed with the move, promoting Ozzel to [[Fleet Admiral/Legends|Fleet Admiral]] and placing him in command of Vader's [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]], the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|Star Dreadnought]] [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']], believing that the man would not be foolish enough to butt heads with the [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]].

His goals having come to fruition, the Admiral was charged with leading the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord's]] [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]] in the search for the headquarters of the Rebel Alliance. Some saw Ozzel as Vader's quasi-equal, but in actuality, he was nothing more than a figurehead&mdash;the true power rested in the hands of Palpatine's [[Sith apprentice/Legends|lieutenant]]. Admiral Ozzel's personality more than often put him at odds with both [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] Vader and his immediate subordinate Captain [[Firmus Piett/Legends|Firmus Piett]], who both considered him inept. Thus, when a [[Viper probe droid/Legends|probe droid]] relayed data of a settlement on the supposedly-uninhabited [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]], Ozzel disagreed with Vader's assertion that they had found the Rebel base. The Dark Lord overruled the admiral in favor of Piett's judgement and ordered the ''Executor'' and Death Squadron to the [[Hoth system/Legends|Hoth system]]. Ozzel attempted to surprise the Alliance by bringing the [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] out of [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] near Hoth rather than approach from the [[Star system/Legends|system's]] outskirts, but the tactical blunder only alerted the Alliance and bought them [[Time/Legends|time]] to raise their [[Echo Base/Legends|base's]] [[Planetary shield/Legends|energy shield]] and evacuate the world. Having tired of the admiral's incompetence, Vader [[Telekinesis/Legends|Force choked]] Ozzel to death.

==Biography==
===Early life===
Kendal Ozzel was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] born on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Carida/Legends|Carida]] into the wealthy [[Ozzel family/Legends|Ozzel family]], a Caridan bloodline brought into wealth by the trading mastermind [[Mann Ozzel]] ages before Kendal's lifetime.<ref name="DB" /> The Ozzel surname was synonymous with proud [[Navy/Legends|naval]] heritage and was counted among the [[Generationals]],<ref name="CSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> and like most families with such prestige, the Ozzels had an estate in the [[Sirpar Hills]] on the planet [[Anaxes/Legends|Anaxes]].<ref name="CCW">''[[Coruscant and the Core Worlds]]''</ref><ref name="Atlas" /> Later in life, Ozzel employed his bloodline as a tool used to rise through the social, [[Politics/Legends|political]], and military ranks of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="DB" />

As the second-born son, Ozzel was unable to inherit his family's business or land;<ref name="The Empire's Finest">{{InsiderCite|96|The Empire's Finest: Who's Who in the Imperial Military}}</ref> instead, he attended multiple [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core World]] institutes<ref name="DB" />&mdash;including the finest naval academy on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]]<ref name="FF4" />&mdash;that catered to the more privileged members of galactic society.<ref name="DB" /> After graduating from the Coruscant naval academy, Ozzel became a [[Captain of the Line/Legends|Captain of the Line]], which would ordinarily entitle him to the command of a [[line of battle]] or a [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]]. His superiors did not see him fit to serve as a field [[Commander/Legends|commander]],<ref name="FF4" /> and, for a while, Ozzel taught at the [[Carida Academy/Legends|Academy of Carida]].<ref name="CSWE" /> He served in the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] during the time of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]], and he was a supporter of then-[[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] rise to power.<ref name="FF4" />

===The Clone Wars===
{{Quote|I saved ''your'' life and acted in the ''interest'' of the Republic, General. Need I remind you that I was awarded this commission by Supreme Chancellor Palpatine himself?|Captain Ozzel, defending his actions on Khorm to Plo Koon|<ref name="TCW7">[[The Clone Wars 7|''The Clone Wars'' 7]]</ref>}}
[[File:Major_Ozzel.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Ozzel's actions on Khorm more often than not put his allies in danger from enemy fire.]]
In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] broke out between the Republic and the breakaway [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], and a [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|clone army]] was established to beat back the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|droid forces]] of the Separatists.<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Ozzel's support of Palpatine earned him a commission as a [[Captain/Legends|captain]] in the new army, commanding the [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] of the [[44th Special Operations Division]], a unit often assigned to destroy enemy targets. He was willing to sacrifice the [[Cloning/Legends|clones]] under his command, including the unit known as the "[[Devil Dogs]]," whom he saw as expendable and easily replaceable.<ref name="TCW7" />

As the war progressed, the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] dispatched Ozzel and his command to the icy planet [[Khorm/Legends|Khorm]] to secure the rare [[Ore/Legends|ore]] [[Agrocite/Legends|agrocite]], which provided [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] with exceptional power. Joined by [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Wieler]]'s group of [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-class Star Destroyers]] and three [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]]&mdash;[[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]], [[Kit Fisto/Legends|Kit Fisto]], and [[Tauht]]&mdash; Captain Ozzel and the Devil Dogs discovered that the native [[Khormai/Legends|Khormai]] [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]], [[Unger Gout]], had allied with the Separatists. A Republic assault force, comprised of [[All Terrain Tactical Enforcer/Legends|AT-TEs]] and [[All Terrain Recon Transport/Legends|AT-RTs]] [[Walker/Legends|walkers]], landed on the planet and proceeded toward the [[Agrocite processing facility|agrocite processing plant]]. En route, Separatist<ref name="TCW7" /> [[J-1 semi-autonomous proton cannon]]s<ref name="Incredible Vehicles">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Incredible Vehicles]]''</ref> [[Battle of Khorm/Legends|opened fire]] on the Republic forces; Ozzel ordered his troops to disembark from the walkers, a tactical maneuver that not only exposed the clones to enemy fire but prompted the three Jedi to draw some of the fire away from the beleaguered soldiers. As the Jedi moved into the [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droid]]-filled trenches, Ozzel ordered his AT-TEs to open fire on the [[Droid/Legends|droids]], endangering the Jedi but wiping out the enemy defenders. The Republic forces succeeded in capturing the processing plant as Gout retreated; although he complained about the temperature, Ozzel was quick to note his part in the victory.<ref name="TCW7" />

Despite this small success, the Republic was still faced with the task of capturing the heavily-fortified agrocite mines. Fisto advised finding an alternative to a direct assault on the mines, but Ozzel stressed that such a move, while costly, was their only option&mdash;while clones would die, more could always be produced to replace the losses. When Koon began to criticize the captain for his overly-aggressive tactics and his disregard for the clones, Ozzel stated that he was merely acting in the interest of the Republic and mentioned how the Chancellor had awarded him a commission as captain. Koon scolded Ozzel, putting him in his place before leaving with Fisto and a squad of [[Clone commando/Legends|clone commandos]] to attack the mines.<ref name="TCW7" />

[[File:Ozzel_charge.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Thrust into command on Khorm, Ozzel nearly cost the Republic its victory.]]
Captain Ozzel's leadership was tested when [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku's]] [[Sith apprentice/Legends|disciple]], [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]], led [[Armored Assault Tank/Legends|Armored Assault Tanks]] in an assault on the processing plant. Initially tasked with holding the Republic lines, he was forced to assume command when the [[Dark Acolyte/Legends|Dark Acolyte]] Ventress killed Master Tauht in a [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|lightsaber duel]]. The captain boarded an AT-TE and ordered a counterattack, pushing forward into a snow-covered canyon where they were ambushed by multiple [[DSD1 dwarf spider droid/Legends|DSD1 dwarf spider droids]]. Faced with the possibility of being killed in action, Ozzel surrendered himself and his clones to the Separatists. Gout and Ventress attempted to interrogate their prisoners, but Ozzel, invoking the [[Convention of Civilized Systems/Legends|Convention of Civilized Systems]], refused to reveal any information&mdash;until an impatient Ventress [[Sai cha/Legends|decapitated]] one of the clone troopers. Frightened at the thought of death, Ozzel gradually betrayed the remaining Jedi's mission to destroy a [[weather-control station]] on a nearby mountain which was preventing any Republic reinforcements from landing. Ventress was prepared to kill the captain, but Gout intervened, suggesting that the prisoners be kept alive for use as [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]]&mdash;or food for slaves&mdash;in accordance with Khormai beliefs regarding prisoners.<ref name="TCW7" /> As the clones busied themselves with finding a way out of their cell, Ozzel attempted to justify his revealing of the Jedi's plans. The captain and the soldiers succeeded in breaking out, hijacking an AAT and cutting down [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droids]] and [[BX-series droid commando/Legends|BX-series droid commandos]] as they made their escape from the facility.<ref name="TCW8">[[The Clone Wars 8|''The Clone Wars'' 8]]</ref>

Upon reuniting with the remnants of the attack force, Ozzel resumed command, believing the Jedi to be dead as a result of his betrayal. The captain ordered that the transports rendezvous with Wieler's fleet for resupplying in preparation for a renewed counterattack, but the ships were frozen in place. Lacking any heavy support, Ozzel's forces were trapped when the Confederacy launched its own attack, and the captain again prepared to surrender to save his own life. Commander Wolffe moved to shield Ozzel, ordering his troops to provide defensive fire as they fell back to the transports. The Jedi&mdash;still alive, no thanks to the captain&mdash;succeeded in destroying the weather-control station in the nick of time, allowing [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry/Legends|LAAT/i]] [[Gunship/Legends|gunships]] and [[V-19 Torrent starfighter/Legends|V-19 Torrent starfighters]] to provide much-needed support to the beleaguered soldiers on the ground. With Ventress forced to retreat, Ozzel once again took the credit for the victory.<ref name="TCW8" />

With reinforcements now available, the Republic forces regrouped in preparation for a final strike on the agrocite mine. As the Jedi performed a reconnaissance of the facility, Ozzel led an aerial attack on the mine, commanding from a LAAT/i gunship. The assortment of V-19 Torrents, [[BTL-B Y-wing starfighter/Legends|BTL-B Y-wings]], gunships, and two [[Acclamator-class transgalactic military assault ship/Legends|''Acclamator''-class assault ships]] made short work of the Separatist defenses, but Gout surprised the Republic with his [[Agrocite cannon|agrocite-powered cannons]], which destroyed the two assault ships in quick succession. In the resulting retreat, Ozzel was knocked unconscious. Despite the setback, Wolffe led the survivors in a successful ground assault on the mines as Fisto destroyed the cannons and killed Gout while Koon forced Ventress to retreat. At the Republic command post following the victory, Ozzel was congratulated by Palpatine via [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] as the surviving clones looked on. The Supreme Chancellor applauded the captain's courageous leadership during the battle<ref name="TCW9">[[The Clone Wars 9|''The Clone Wars'' 9]]</ref> and awarded him his own ship and fighter group.<ref name="TCWTPB">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: In Service of the Republic]]''</ref>

===Ambitions===
{{Quote|You really think she maneuvered herself aboard this ship and into the computer without already knowing what she was looking for?''"<br />"''She ''maneuvered'' herself aboard? Including setting up a pirate attack on an Imperial-chartered freighter?''"<br />"''Special Imperial agents don't bother with anything as trivial as pirates. And the Emperor's Hand ''certainly'' doesn't. If she happened to foil a pirate attack, it was purely incidental to her main mission.|Ozzel and Somoril discuss Mara Jade's presence aboard the ''Reprisal''|<ref name="Allegiance">[[Allegiance (novel)|''Allegiance'']]</ref>}}
[[File:OzzelSansMoustache-AllegianceJP.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Because of Mara Jade's suspicions, Ozzel was eventually transferred from the ''Reprisal'' to the ''Executor''.]]
Captain Ozzel continued to serve in the military following [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] Palpatine's [[Declaration of a New Order|reorganization]] of the Republic into the Empire.<ref name="FF4" /> In [[5 BBY/Legends|5 BBY]], Ozzel was the presiding officer at the court-martial for Imperial [[Cadet/Legends|cadet]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], who had saved the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] from slavery. At the trial, the young [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] took a fairly low view of Ozzel's intelligence.<ref name="Hutt" /> For a short time, Ozzel served as an instructor at the [[Imperial Naval Academy (Coruscant)|Naval Academy]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], where he taught naval history and languages<ref name="FF4" /> until the destruction of the Empire's [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] during the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].<ref name="The Empire's Finest" /> Around this time, Ozzel was also involved in codifying the tactics of the Imperial Navy, and he recorded his thoughts on the subject in a treatise he titled ''[[Innovations in Imperial Naval Tactics]]'', which identified the three principles of "Surprise", "Pursue", and "Overwhelm" as being at the heart of naval tactics. Han Solo would later regard Ozzel's "innovations" as being comically simplistic, but Ozzel's treatise was later included in the official field guide for officers in the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]], ''[[Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''.<ref name="SW:IH:ACG" />

In [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], Ozzel was serving as captain of the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]] [[Reprisal (Imperial II-class)|''Reprisal'']], the largest [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]] in the [[Shelsha sector/Legends|Shelsha sector]]. At the planet [[Teardrop]], the site of a covert [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] listening post, he initiated a blockade to prevent any Rebels from fleeing the world. Han Solo&mdash;now a [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] affiliated with the Alliance&mdash;attempted to flee the world with Rebel passengers in his [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|freighter]], the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']], but his [[Starship/Legends|ship]] fell under attack by [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]]. Solo requested aid from the Star Destroyer, and Ozzel had his [[Gunner/Legends|gunners]] fire upon and destroy the attackers. Solo claimed that his ship, using the alias "''Argos''," had carried a [[Briston]]-based medical relief team responding to a [[Groundquake/Legends|groundquake]] on Teardrop's [[Por'ste Island]]. Ozzel, believing Solo's cover story, ordered the ship back to Briston, but the [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] left the [[Teardrop system/Legends|system]] with its cargo of Rebels. Ozzel later oversaw the [[Teardrop massacre|massacre]] of "Rebel sympathizers" on the planet, where Imperial troops killed all the civilians in a town, [[Alien/Legends|aliens]] first. This massacre, ordered by [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]] [[Major/Legends|Major]] [[Drelfin]], was blamed on Rebel agitators present in the town, who had in fact already fled the world aboard the ''Falcon''. Six days later, the ''Reprisal'' was assigned a full Imperial Security Bureau [[tactical unit]] under the command of [[Colonel/Legends|Colonel]] [[Vak Somoril]], to further prosecute the suppression of resistance in the sector.<ref name="Allegiance" />

[[Stormtrooper/Legends|Stormtrooper]] [[Daric LaRone]] later confronted Drelfin about the killing of civilians on Teardrop, and, after a brief struggle that resulted in the major's [[Death/Legends|death]], LaRone fled the ''Reprisal'' with a [[Hand of Judgment|group of fellow stormtroopers]] who had witnessed the killing. [[Emperor's Hand/Legends|Emperor's Hand]] [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]] had been investigating a group of pirates known as the [[BloodScar]]s in the Shelsha [[Sector/Legends|sector]] in connection to six stolen paintings found in [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Glovstoak]]'s possession, and when she arrived aboard the ''Reprisal'', Captain Ozzel and Colonel Somoril mistakenly believed that her arrival was part of a high-level investigation into the incident regarding the rogue stormtroopers. To cover up the incident, they conspired in an unsanctioned scheme to kill her after discovering that she had accessed the ship's personnel files, [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]] log, and flight log. The captain was certain that an [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor's]] Hand wouldn't be sent on a trivial mission to eliminate pirates, and he believed that her main mission was to investigate the stormtroopers who deserted. Ozzel realized the repercussions of killing such an Imperial agent would be great, but Somoril managed to convince the captain to head for the [[Gepparin system/Legends|Gepparin system]] to [[Bombing of Gepparin|attack]] the pirate base where Jade had gone after departing the destroyer. The colonel's reasoning was that Imperial agents, even an Emperor's Hand, could easily end up somewhere during a military strike and be killed. Ozzel only agreed because he didn't want the desertion of the stormtroopers to get in the way of his ultimate goal of achieving the rank of admiral. The plan failed, when Ozzel chose to follow the ''Millennium Falcon'', piloted by Solo's copilot, Chewbacca, rather than complete the attack on the pirate base. Ozzel had the ''Reprisal'' jump to the [[Alderaan system/Legends|Alderaan system]] in an effort to pursue the freighter, but he was unsuccessful in intercepting them. Jade was ultimately unable to prove Ozzel's complicity, but she suggested that [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], [[Supreme Commander (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Supreme Commander]] of the Imperial Military,<ref name="kenner">{{KennerCite|set=Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (toy line)|pack=Darth Vader vs. Prince Xizor|link=soteKxizor-vader.asp}}</ref> keep a close eye on the captain.<ref name="Allegiance" />

===Ascent===
{{Quote|What would you like me to do?''"<br />"''I'm not really sure. Keep an eye on Ozzel, I suppose. I don't know if the man's disloyal, easily manipulated, or just plain stupid. But I think he bears watching.|Darth Vader and Mara Jade|<ref name="Allegiance" />}}
[[File:OzzelIsSmarterThanYou-ESBHD.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Ozzel was appointed commander of Death Squadron because many believed he would not argue with Vader, which he did on several occasions.]]
Promoted to [[Fleet Admiral/Legends|Fleet Admiral]]<ref name="The Empire's Finest" /> as a result of Mara Jade's suggestion,<ref name="Allegiance" /> Ozzel had unexpectedly achieved his goal. He was assigned as the commanding officer of the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|''Executor''-class Star Dreadnought]] [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']],<ref name="The Empire's Finest" /> the flagship of the Supreme Commander,<ref name="kenner" /> Darth Vader himself.<ref name="The Empire's Finest" /> Strong ties to [[Imperial High Command/Legends|Imperial High Command]] allowed Ozzel to take command of Vader's [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]], but many believed that this was merely a political move;<ref name="CSWE" /> Ozzel's promotion had coincided with the death of his predecessor, [[Amise Griff]]<ref name="The Empire's Finest" /> and the loss of a cadre of able officers aboard the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]].<ref name="DB" /> In fact, naval hierarchy had given Ozzel his command because they believed he wasn't stupid enough to quarrel with Vader, who was the squadron's true commander.<ref name="FF4" /> When he was first made admiral, many officers saw him as holding status quasi-equal to the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]], but speculation abounded as to the exact nature by which Ozzel achieved his prestigious command position. Many believed older ties between Imperial Command and Ozzel's bloodline were chiefly responsible for his sudden and inexplicable rise, or that he was merely acting as a figurehead of command in Vader's fleet to appease the high-ranking members of the general staff.<ref name="GG3">''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref> Indeed, Ozzel was primarily Vader's puppet,<ref name="FF19">{{FactFile|19|VAD 7-12|Darth Vader}}</ref> wielding little power in comparison to the Supreme Commander.<ref name="FF4" /> Captain [[Firmus Piett/Legends|Firmus Piett]], a fleet officer who had previously served under Admiral Griff,<ref name="GG3" /> became Admiral Ozzel's senior subordinate aboard the ''Executor''.<ref name="The Empire's Finest" />

Early into Ozzel's command of the ''Executor'', he was assigned to patrol the [[Black Widow Nebula/Legends|Black Widow Nebula]] in search for a [[Corvette/Legends|corvette]] commanded by the renegade Imperial Captain [[Sodarra]].<ref name="CSWE" /> While there, the ''Millennium Falcon'' was captured by the ''Executor'', and Ozzel interrogated its captain, Han Solo, on the bridge of the [[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]] about his presence in the nebula.<ref name="Scoundrel's Luck">In ''[[Scoundrel's Luck]]'', Ozzel appears only if the player decides to bribe Captain Piett, who leads a boarding party onto the ''Millennium Falcon''.</ref> At one point, Solo alluded to the corvette, and Ozzel decided to let the ''Falcon'' escape, hoping that Solo would lead the Empire to Sodarra and his fellow deserters.<ref name="CSWE" />

===Hunt for the Rebel headquarters===
{{Quote|I think we've got something, sir. The report is only a fragment from a probe droid in the Hoth system, but it's the best lead we've had.''"<br />"''We have thousands of probe droids searching the galaxy. I want proof, not leads!|Firmus Piett and Kendal Ozzel|audio=PiettOzzelBestLead-TESB.flac|<ref name="TESB" />}}
[[File:LaurelAndHardyJoinTheImperialNavy-EGW.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Ozzel, joined by Captain Piett, oversaw a substantial force of Imperial warships while searching for the Rebel headquarters.]]
Under Vader's supervision, Ozzel was tasked with hunting down the headquarters of the [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]] using whatever devices he deemed necessary. As their hunt for the Rebel base continued, Ozzel and Piett came to despise one another. The admiral was alternately impetuous and languorous: in the case of the former, he took a personal approach to his mission, preferring to follow up on substantial leads himself. This often meant diverting the fleet on less-than-productive forays, which soon earned the ire of [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader, who grew tired of these indulgences. In the case of the latter, he dismissed reports of uncharted settlements on a whim and ridiculed his subordinates' ideas and findings to protect his position. A staunch professional, Piett regarded Ozzel as too incompetent to be trusted with the task of destroying the Rebellion, and began thinking about how to engineer the Admiral's downfall.<ref name="Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> Meanwhile, an exasperated Vader relegated Ozzel to the position of figurehead that he effectively occupied, serving merely as a go-between for issuing the Supreme Commander's orders to the ''Executor''{{'s}} rank and file.<ref name="GG3" /> On one occasion, Ozzel personally escorted [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Janek Sunber/Legends|Janek Sunber]] to Vader's [[Darth Vader's meditation chamber/Legends|meditation chamber]], where the lieutenant was received by Palpatine's right-hand man.<ref name="Rebellion 1">[[Rebellion 1|''Rebellion'' 1]]</ref>

Shortly thereafter, Ozzel and Vader led the ''Executor'' and Death Squadron into a [[Disaster at Deepspace Besh|battle against the Rebel fleet]]<ref name="Rebellion 5">[[Rebellion 5|''Rebellion'' 5]]</ref> at [[Tingel Deepspace Besh]]<ref name="Atlas" /> a few months after the Battle of Yavin. As the Rebels' escape algorithm had been uncovered by the Empire, Imperial forces were waiting at the next prearranged Rebel rendezvous point should the fleet attempt an escape. Unaware that the Alliance had learned of this breach, Ozzel believed that the battle would bring about the end of the Rebellion. The engagement decimated the Rebel fleet, but the Alliance forces scattered in several different directions rather than use the compromised algorithm, depriving Vader of a definitive victory. Following the battle, Ozzel reported that [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]] had detected an [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pod]] from the Alliance flagship, ''[[Rebel One]]''.<ref name="Rebellion 5" />

In [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]], Admiral Ozzel was present at the commissioning ceremony for the ''Executor'' at the [[Imperial Transfer Post]] near the planet [[Kuat/Legends|Kuat]], joining Emperor Palpatine, [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] Vader, and an array of naval personnel including [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Rufaan Tigellinus]] and Admirals [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]], [[Tandres]], and [[Tavares]]. It was at this time that the Super Star Destroyer, which had been in service for some time and just completed its shakedown cruise, officially joined with Death Squadron. Ozzel transferred his flag to the ''Executor'' as well,<ref name="Journal12">{{JournalCite|12|Galaxywide NewsNets}}</ref> even though he had commanded the warship since 0.5 ABY.<ref name="Allegiance" /> After this, about a [[Standard month/Legends|month]] before [[Fete Week|New Year's Fete Week]] in 38:F1, Vader departed from [[Galactic City/Legends|Imperial City]] on Coruscant to officially begin his oversight of Ozzel and Death Squadron.<ref name="Journal13">{{JournalCite|13|Galaxywide NewsNets}}</ref>

[[File:YouSuckPiett-ESBHD.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Over time, Ozzel and Piett came to despise one another, with the latter scheming to replace the former.]]
As the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] progressed, Ozzel and his command were tasked with rooting out and destroying any elements of the Rebel Alliance in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]]. In their surveillance of remote [[Star system/Legends|star systems]], it was reported by the [[Independent Traders' Infonet/Legends|Independent Traders' Infonet]] that Star Destroyers under Ozzel's command apprehended a number of [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] in the systems and briefly detained them for questioning as the admiral searched for any potential leads regarding Rebel activity in the area. Death Squadron adopted a hostile approach to both the Rebellion and its suspected sympathizers&mdash;as reported by the [[Nal Hutta Kal'tamok/Legends|''Nal Hutta Kal'tamok'']], it was believed that the destruction of the [[Syvris/Legends|Syvris]] [[Shadowport/Legends|shadowport]] was carried out by Star Destroyers under Ozzel's command, having mistaken the shadowport for a Rebel facility.<ref name="Journal13" />

During his tenure as admiral, Ozzel assigned command of the [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] [[Avenger/Legends|''Avenger'']] to Captain [[Lorth Needa/Legends|Lorth Needa]], who became one of Ozzel's closest [[Advisor/Legends|advisors]].<ref name="Needa card">{{CCG|set=Dagobah Limited|cardname=Captain Needa}}</ref> The admiral placed a great deal of trust in Needa, tasking the captain with taking the ''Avenger'' to check on various leads in the search for the Rebel command base. Furthermore, Ozzel assigned the ''Avenger'' to the prestigious point position of Death Squadron.<ref name="GG3" /> Vader, as well as his [[Sith Master/Legends|master]], Palpatine, came to distrust the admiral and his closest associates, Needa included.<ref name="Needa card" /> Should one of them make even the most minor of mistakes, the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] would execute the individual as a consequence for failing.<ref name="GG3" />

By [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], Death Squadron had scoured a large area of space in its search for the Rebel headquarters, to no avail. In an effort to speed up the process, Ozzel authorized the deployment of [[Arakyd Industries/Legends|Arakyd]] [[Viper probe droid/Legends|Viper probe droids]], dispersing them throughout the galaxy with the hope that one would stumble upon the main Alliance base. The admiral requested that additional vessels be assigned to Death Squadron to complement those warships already under his command, but because of the rising amount of support for the Rebellion in the galaxy, no ships were available to fulfill Ozzel's appeal.<ref name="A Question of Survival">{{ESBRadio|A Question of Survival}}</ref> The probe droids uncovered large numbers of uncharted settlements, including [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]]' nests, which forced Death Squadron to respond to dozens of false alarms that Vader quickly became tired of.<ref name="TESB" /><ref name="Warfare" />

===Final failure===
{{Quote|Lord Vader, the fleet has moved out of lightspeed, and we're preparing to&mdash;''"<br />"''You have failed me for the last time, Admiral.|Ozzel reports to Vader, mere moments before his execution|audio=YouHaveFailedMeForTheLastTime-TESB.flac|<ref name="TESB" />}}
Death Squadron's search for the Rebel headquarters ended when a [[Probe droid/Legends|probe droid]]<ref name="TESB" /> launched from the Star Destroyer ''[[Stalker/Legends|Stalker]]''<ref name="Stalker CCG">{{CCG|set=Hoth Limited|cardname=''Stalker''}}</ref> discovered signs of occupancy on the otherwise-uninhabited planet of [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]], in the [[Hoth system/Legends|system of the same name]]. The droid transmitted its findings, which included the presence of a [[Power generator/Legends|power generator]] on the world, back to the ''Executor'', where it was reviewed by Piett.<ref name="TESB" /> Piett, having grown tired of Ozzel blaming his own mistakes on his subordinates, had been scheming to discredit the admiral and replace him at Vader's side in Death Squadron. As such, the captain decided to bypass his commanding officer completely with news of the discovery. Believing that Ozzel would ignore the intelligence, Piett waited until Vader was on the bridge to tell the admiral, hoping that such a move would expedite Ozzel's removal from command.<ref name="GG3" /><ref name="Warfare" />

[[File:Ozzel_croaks.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Having grown tired of Ozzel's repeated failures, Vader telekinetically executed the admiral just prior to the Battle of Hoth.]]
When Piett did inform Ozzel of the data from Hoth, the admiral responded<ref name="TESB" /> as the captain had predicted<ref name="GG3" />&mdash;he disregarded the findings as another lead lacking any validity. He believed that the droid had stumbled upon a settlement of smugglers, and not the long-sought-after Rebel base. The Supreme Commander overheard and disagreed with the admiral's interpretation of the facts. With certainty, Vader announced that Hoth was housing the Alliance headquarters.<ref name="TESB" /><ref name="Warfare" /> Ozzel, still not convinced, asked Piett to consult the [[intelligence evaluation computer]]s on the matter; the computers reported that the data index on a Rebel presence on Hoth was low, and Ozzel insolently tried to convince Vader that the finding might simply be a smuggler base. [[The Force/Legends|The Force]] told Vader all he needed to know&mdash;the Rebels were on the planet, and [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], for whom he had long searched, was with them.<ref name="A Question of Survival" /> The Dark Lord ordered Death Squadron into [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]], the sixth world of the Hoth system their destination.<ref name="TESB" />

Ozzel took some liberties with Vader's command. Believing that a sudden appearance of an Imperial fleet would catch the Alliance off-guard, he brought Death Squadron out of [[Lightspeed/Legends|lightspeed]] in close proximity to Hoth, rather than emerge in the outskirts of the system. This surprise allowed the Rebels at [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] to raise an [[Planetary shield/Legends|energy shield]] strong enough to withstand any [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|orbital bombardment]] initiated by the [[Orbit/Legends|orbiting]] Star Destroyers. [[General/Legends|General]] [[Maximilian Veers/Legends|Maximilian Veers]] brought word of the ramifications of Admiral Ozzel's decision to Lord Vader, who viewed his subordinate as inept for executing such a maneuver.<ref name="TESB" /> Realizing that Death Squadron would now have to waste its resources in fighting a costly [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|ground battle]] rather than simply destroying the base from orbit as a result of the admiral's actions, Vader contacted Ozzel from his meditation chamber aboard the ''Executor''. Via a [[Viewscreen/Legends|viewscreen]], Ozzel announced that the fleet had arrived in the Hoth system, but his report was cut short when Vader began to [[Telekinesis/Legends#Choking powers|Force Choke]] the admiral as punishment for his blunder. Deciding that the man had made his final mistake, and that simply punishing him would be pointless,<ref name="Fire and Ice">{{ESBRadio|Fire and Ice}}</ref> Vader executed Ozzel and immediately promoted Piett to fill the vacancy Ozzel's death had created.<ref name="TESB" />

===Legacy===
As a result of Ozzel's fatal decision, Death Squadron was forced to wage a ground battle against the Rebel defenders of Echo Base, one that ultimately proved successful despite minor Imperial casualties. Skywalker and his allies successfully fled from the Imperial forces, depriving Vader of a complete victory on Hoth.<ref name="TESB" /> Following the engagement, the admiral's remains were transported back to his homeworld<ref name="Journal14">{{JournalCite|14|Galaxywide NewsNets}}</ref> of Carida,<ref name="Homeworld">{{JournalCite|14|Galaxywide NewsNets}}&mdash;The article states that Ozzel was honored at the [[Corulag Academy]] on his homeworld, implying that he was born on [[Corulag/Legends|Corulag]], the site of the academy. The [[StarWars.com]] [[Databank (original)|Databank]] established Carida as his homeworld. This article assumes that the ''Adventure Journal'' article is in error.</ref> where he was honored at a ceremony. Imperial propaganda compiled by [[Imperial Advisor/Legends|Imperial advisor]] [[Alec Pradeux]] on the Battle of Hoth greatly altered the circumstances of Ozzel's death, removing Vader's involvement in this "official" account. Pradeux instead claimed that the admiral had been killed when Rebel forces bombarded the ''Executor'' with a planetary energy emplacement.<ref name="Journal14" />

Later that year, before his own execution by [[High Inquisitor]] [[Antinnis Tremayne]], Captain [[Jovan Vharing]] of the Star Destroyer [[Interrogator/Legends|''Interrogator'']] recalled Admiral Ozzel as one of many naval personnel who had been executed for failure by their superiors.<ref name="Journal11">{{JournalCite|11|The Longest Fall}}</ref> A few months after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], a copy of the ''Imperial Handbook'' was captured by the Rebel Alliance and delivered to the Alliance High Command by Skywalker. The copy included Ozzel's ''Innovations in Imperial Naval Tactics''. Solo, when reading through the innovations, noted that they were so poorly thought out that he simply could not make fun of it due to being far too easy to do so.<ref name="SW:IH:ACG" /> In [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]], the smuggler [[Starter]] claimed to have been unsuccessfully interrogated by Ozzel aboard the ''Executor''. When recounting his tale, which few believed, Starter claimed that Ozzel went through five [[Interrogation droid/Legends|interrogation droids]] before reporting to Vader of his failure.<ref name="Journal4">{{JournalCite|4|Starter's Tale}}</ref>

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|The Rebels are alerted to our presence. Admiral Ozzel came out of lightspeed too close to the system.''"<br />"''He felt surprise was wiser&hellip;''"<br />"''He is as clumsy as he is stupid.|Vader expresses his displeasure with Ozzel to General Veers|<ref name="TESB" />}}
[[File:AdmiralOzzel-TotC.jpg|thumb|right|Ozzel was looked down upon by many of his contemporaries.]]
A by-the-books officer,<ref name="CSWE" /> Kendal Ozzel was generally viewed unfavorably, considered inept by many Imperials and others. There was a vast array of uncharitable opinions on the officer; BloodScar [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] [[Caaldra]] saw Ozzel as predictable, while Mara Jade was unable to tell if he was treacherous, easily manipulated, or simply dim-witted.<ref name="Allegiance" /> His superiors at the Coruscant naval academy were loath to give him a position of command.<ref name="FF4" /> When on the verge of defeat on the battlefield, Ozzel opted to surrender rather than risk death in continued combat. If he were to be interrogated, Ozzel preferred to betray his allies to the enemy rather than risk execution,<ref name="TCW7" /> attempting to justify his betrayal to himself later on.<ref name="TCW8" /> His subordinate and successor, Firmus Piett, found Ozzel to be mercurial and considered him too incompetent for his command.<ref name="Warfare" /> These traits made many wonder how he achieved his rank of admiral.<ref name="DB" /> Han Solo, who already had very low opinions of Ozzel, also admitted when reading his ''Innovations in Imperial Naval Tactics'' that his "innovations" were so bad that he was unwilling to mock him precisely because it would have been too easy to do so.<ref name="SW:IH:ACG" /> Darth Vader shared this opinion of him throughout Ozzel's time as admiral, especially when he brought Death Squadron out of hyperspace too close to Hoth, a move with which the admiral had hoped would surprise the Alliance. Because of his actions, the Alliance was able to detect the fleet of approaching Star Destroyers, activate Echo Base's shield, and evacuate the majority of the base.<ref name="TESB" />

Ozzel was also noted as being argumentative, bullish, and lacking common sense&mdash;additional traits which often caused further problems. He never knew when to be quiet, and he always insisted on having a say in major decisions. He was a disciplinarian, and every detail had to be perfect. His tactical thinking was outdated, and his presence aboard the ''Executor'' was in part to satisfy the Navy's senior commanders and show a small amount of respect with regards to the chain-of-command, even though Vader, as Supreme Commander,<ref name="kenner" /> held ''de facto'' command of Death Squadron.<ref name="FF4" /> He was known to ridicule the ideas and findings of his subordinates to protect his own position.<ref name="Warfare" /> Ozzel let off-duty stormtroopers roam around without their [[Stormtrooper armor/Legends|armor]] on while serving aboard the ''Reprisal'', which went against regulations. He did not like their presence on the ship, so he reached this unofficial agreement with the stormtrooper commanders, rather than having the troops confined to the [[Barracks/Legends|barracks]].<ref name="Allegiance" /> He was also biased against women and [[Non-huMan|non-Humans]]<ref name="FF4" /> and intimidated lesser bureaucrats to increase his standing in the Navy.<ref name="The Empire's Finest" />

Despite these flaws, Ozzel was a self-confident and ambitious man,<ref name="Allegiance" /> often using his family name to further himself in Imperial society and politics.<ref name="DB" /> He was considered the ideal naval politician, and as far as he was concerned, he always won his arguments. He viewed the elimination of Rebels as the fastest path to success within the Imperial Navy, and he hoped that his attempt to destroy the Rebels would eventually grant him the rank of admiral.<ref name="Allegiance" /> His ambition was such that, moments before his death, he implied a desire to take over the Empire using the ''Executor''.<ref name="New Vehicles & Vessels" /> Whenever he failed he would cast the blame onto his subordinates, which sparked an enmity between him and his subordinate and eventual replacement, Firmus Piett.<ref name="GG3" /> Ozzel was willing to go to extreme measures to cover his mistakes, such as when he reluctantly agreed to kill Emperor's Hand Mara Jade to silence potential information on the desertion of stormtroopers from the ''Reprisal''.<ref name="Allegiance" /> He was confident, and he felt relaxed while in the presence of Vader,<ref name="ESB novel">[[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back'' novelization]]</ref> whom he came to resent over time.<ref name="GG3" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Ozzel_lookalike-CSW.jpg|thumb|left|150px|The Ozzel lookalike from Marvel ''Star Wars.'']]
===Portrayal and origins===
Kendal Ozzel first appeared in [[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|''The Empire Strikes Back'' novelization]]<ref name="ESB novel" /> and ''[[The Empire Strikes Back Storybook]]'',<ref name="Storybook">''[[The Empire Strikes Back Storybook]]''</ref> both released on [[April 12]], [[1980]].<ref name="ESB novel" /><ref name="Storybook" /> In [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']], Ozzel was played by [[Michael Sheard]].<ref name="The Empire's Finest" /> In the [[The Empire Strikes Back (radio)|audio drama version]] of ''The Empire Strikes Back'', Ozzel was voiced by [[Peter Michael Goetz]].<ref name="A Question of Survival" /> The admiral went without a first name until ''[[The Official Star Wars Fact File 4]]'' supplied the forename "Kendal,"<ref name="FF4" /> which was used with Sheard's blessing.<ref name="interview">{{WebCite|url=http://www.michaelsheard.com/interviews/johnj.htm|text=Interview with Michael Sheard|archivedate=20010822053425}}</ref> The name later made its way to the official Star Wars website's [[Databank (original)|Databank]].<ref name="DB" />

===Continuity issues===
Ozzel's role varies from adaptation to adaptation of ''The Empire Strikes Back''. In both the official novelization and ''The Empire Strikes Back Storybook'', Ozzel's dialogue is altered slightly.<ref name="ESB novel" /><ref name="Storybook" /> Divergent dialogue can also be found in the radio adaptation.<ref name="A Question of Survival" /> In the [[Classic Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (Random House)|''Classic Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back'' book]], Ozzel appears once, in an altered version of the scene in which the probe droid's findings are analyzed. In this version, Ozzel goes unnamed, and his lines differ from his dialogue in the film.<ref name="Random House">[[Classic Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (Random House)|''Classic Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back'' novelization]]</ref> In both [[Star Wars (1977) 39|''Star Wars'' (1977) 39]] and [[Star Wars (1977) 40|''Star Wars'' (1977) 40]], artist [[Al Williamson]] incorrectly switches Ozzel's and Piett's roles.<ref name="Marvel 39">[[Star Wars (1977) 39|''Star Wars'' (1977) 39]]</ref><ref name="Marvel 40">[[Star Wars (1977) 40|''Star Wars'' (1977) 40]]</ref> Additionally, for ''Star Wars 40'', Williamson and [[Carlos Garzón|Carlos Garzon]] used reference photography of Lorth Needa's death for Ozzel's own death, so the two panels in which the scene is displayed greatly differ from the movie.<ref name="Star Wars 40 mistake">{{SWArchive|url=eu/lit/comics/f20080227/index.html?page=7|text=Checklist: Turning Star Wars Japanese &mdash; Manga Scenes Done Better: Episode V: Death of Admiral Ozzel}}</ref>

[[File:Ozzel_death.png|thumb|250px|Lorth Needa's death, reused for Ozzel's death in ''Star Wars 40: The Empire Strikes Back: Battleground Hoth.'']]
Issues involving Ozzel's rank at certain periods of time have existed. Originally, in the story arc [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: In Service of the Republic|''The Clone Wars: In the Service of the Republic'']] he held the rank of major. At the end of [[The Clone Wars 9|''The Clone Wars'' 9]], Palpatine promotes Ozzel to the rank of admiral for his part in the Battle of Khorm. [[Randy Stradley]] has stated that though this is true to the original script, [[Leland Chee]] left him a note informing him that the rank should be changed from admiral to captain, to coincide with Ozzel's rank of captain in the novel [[Allegiance (novel)|''Allegiance'']]. Though the error was not fixed in time for the comic's release,<ref name="DH message board">{{DHBoards|subdomain=www|url=Help/Boards/viewtopic.php?t=16206|thread=THE CLONE WARS #9 -- Ice on fire!|user=Randy Stradley|date=2009-09-17|time=8:11 am}}</ref> the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: In Service of the Republic (trade paperback)|''In Service of the Republic'' trade paperback]] has Ozzel's rank changed from a major to a captain throughout the story and has him awarded his own ship and fighter group instead of any promotion.<ref name="TCWTPB" />

Similarly, there have been several inconsistencies between the various sources describing Ozzel's path to becoming Vader's senior subordinate in Death Squadron. Going by in-universe chronology, the next source of confusion after ''In Service of the Republic'' is ''[[The Hutt Gambit]]'', which establishes Ozzel as an admiral at the time of Han Solo's trial in 5 BBY.<ref name="Hutt">''[[The Hutt Gambit]]''</ref> The [[2007]] article ''[[The Empire's Finest: Who's Who in the Imperial Military]]'', from [[Star Wars Insider 96|''Star Wars Insider'' 96]], implies that Ozzel served aboard the ''Executor'' under Amise Griff's command, "[seizing] captaincy of Darth Vader's Super Star Destroyer ''Executor''" before "[taking] over as admiral of Vader's Death Squadron following the death of Admiral Griff."<ref name="The Empire's Finest" /> Ozzel later appears as an admiral aboard the ''Executor'' under Vader's command in the canonical path of ''[[Scoundrel's Luck]]'', which apparently takes place while Vader is still in a healing trance in his [[TIE Advanced x1/Legends|TIE Advanced x1]] after the Battle of Yavin.<ref name="Scoundrel's Luck" /> In a NewsNet article in [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 12|''Star Wars Adventure Journal'' 12]], it is mentioned that Ozzel was in command of Death Squadron before the ''Executor'' was commissioned and planned to transfer his flag to the new warship when it entered active service with Death Squadron.<ref name="Journal12" /> These are seemingly contradicted by ''Allegiance'', which establishes Ozzel as the captain of the Star Destroyer ''Reprisal'' (and not an admiral tasked with leading Death Squadron in any way) while the ''Executor'' is active and under the command of Admiral [[Bentro]].<ref name="Allegiance" /> To further add to the confusion, an [[Unidentified Imperial admiral (Executor)|unidentified ''Executor'' admiral]] bearing a remarkable similarity to Ozzel appears in a minor role in the ''[[Classic Star Wars]]'' comics "[[It's a Trap]]" and ''[[Doom Mission]]'', both of which take place before Ozzel's reassignment to the ''Executor''.<ref name="Revenge">"[[It's a Trap]]"</ref><ref name="Doom">"[[Doom Mission]]"</ref>

In [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 14|''Star Wars Adventure Journal'' 14]], it is said that, following Ozzel's death, his remains were returned to his homeworld, where he was honored at the [[Corulag Academy]]. This would imply that Ozzel was born on [[Corulag/Legends|Corulag]], the location of the aforementioned academy.<ref name="Journal14" /> However, Ozzel's Databank entry has established Carida as his homeworld.<ref name="DB" /> This article assumes that the ''Adventure Journal'' is in error.

Though Ozzel dies in ''The Empire Strikes Back'' film and most of its literary adaptation, he survives Vader's wrath in the non-canonical children book ''[[Vader's Little Princess]]''. In the book, during the scene in which Vader was to choke Ozzel for his failure at Hoth, the young Leia appears, leading Vader to change his mind and decides to not choke Ozzel in Leia's presence, at least with her around.<ref name="Vader's Little Princess">''[[Vader's Little Princess]]''</ref>
